=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- tests/test_plan_clarify_blocked_output.py:522 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_steps()` unpacks all workflow jobs as a single job. The PR adds a `heal-report` job to `clarify.yml` and `plan.yml`, so those workflows now have two jobs. The tuple unpack raises `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1)`.
  WHY: CI confirms the crash: `test_clarify_loop_falls_back_to_codex_in_the_same_attempt` calls `_steps("clarify.yml")` → unpacking fails. `test_engine_steps_resolve_the_role_and_guard_the_credential` would also fail for both `clarify.yml` and `plan.yml`. The test file runs as a script (`raise SystemExit(main())`), so the first `_steps` call aborts before any test runs. The CI log shows the exact traceback in `tests-promote-stall-and-review`.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:244–251 (log-fetch failure writes placeholder), 304–313 (fingerprint dispatch relies on LOG_FILES emptiness) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When job-log fetch fails, line 249 writes `(job log unavailable)` into `${FILTERED_LOG}` and line 251 appends it to `LOG_FILES`. At line 304, `[ "${#LOG_FILES[@]}" -gt 0 ]` is true because the placeholder file exists, so the code takes the `error-signature` path, which returns `no-error-lines`. The `phase_failure` fallback at line 310 (`SIGNATURE="phase:${FAILURE_REASON:-unknown}"`) is never reached.
  WHY: A phase-failure report whose job log cannot be fetched gets fingerprinted as `no-error-lines` instead of `phase:plan_failed` (or similar). Different phase failures with missing logs then share the same generic fingerprint, breaking deduplication — a subsequent different failure hits the duplicate path and is recorded as an occurrence comment instead of opening a new heal issue.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:130-132 (PHASE_FAILURE_COMMENT_PREFIXES includes cancellation comments for clarify and implement; plan has only one prefix that covers both failure and cancellation) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Cancelled runs are counted as failed runs in the phase-failure streak.
  WHY: With a threshold of 2, a cancelled run followed by a true failure produces a streak of 2, dispatching a report after only one genuine failure. The `heal-report` job itself correctly gates on `failure` (not `cancelled`), so the report is only generated on real failures, but the streak counter inflates the count. At the default threshold of 1 this has no effect since every failure reports anyway; it only matters when an operator sets a higher threshold to leave first failures to the stall poller.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_phase_report.sh:122-125 (fetches comment bodies only, no author filtering) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The streak counter trusts comment-body prefixes without verifying the comment author. A user can post a body starting with a success prefix (e.g. `The task appears clear.`) to reset the streak count.
  WHY: With threshold above 1, a user-injected success comment breaks the streak, suppressing a report for a subsequent genuine failure. Existing failure-comment counters in the autofix path have the same property (comments are not author-verified), so this follows the repo's existing pattern; exploited only by a user who can already comment on the issue.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- tests/test_plan_clarify_blocked_output.py:(job,) = data["jobs"].values() in _steps() | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The _steps() helper assumes each workflow has exactly one job. The PR adds a second job (heal-report) to clarify.yml and plan.yml, causing a ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1).
  WHY: CI tests crash on import/execution, preventing verification.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:phase_failure_streak() | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Streak calculation includes "cancelled" runs as "failures" and does not distinguish workflow-authored success markers from user comments, and successful implementation runs lack success markers.
  WHY: Streak accumulates incorrectly, leading to false-positive phase_failure reports when runs were not consecutive failures.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:fingerprinting logic | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The phase fingerprint fallback does not run when a job exists but its log cannot be fetched.
  WHY: The "no-error-lines" placeholder makes the fingerprint too generic, causing inaccurate classification of phase_failure reports.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml:Staging loop for f in ... | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: codex_stall_guard.sh is staged but unused in clarify.yml.
  WHY: Unnecessary overhead and potential for failure if the file is missing in the support ref, violating the minimal change set rule (§9).

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- tests/test_plan_clarify_blocked_output.py:`_steps()` lines 520-523 unpacks `data["jobs"].values()` as a single job. The new `heal-report` jobs are at `.github/workflows/clarify.yml:1605` and `.github/workflows/plan.yml:2357`. | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test helper still assumes these workflows have exactly one job.
  WHY: `_steps("clarify.yml")` raises `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1)`. The supplied CI log confirms this failure in `tests-promote-stall-and-review`, causing the CI aggregate check to fail.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:`PHASE_FAILURE_COMMENT_PREFIXES` at lines 129-132 and streak counting at lines 684-695; `.github/workflows/plan.yml:2312-2323` posts the same failure-prefixed comment when the job is cancelled. | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Cancelled runs are counted as failed runs. Clarify and implement also include cancellation-comment prefixes in the counted failure prefixes.
  WHY: With `WORKFLOW_HEAL_PHASE_FAILURE_STREAK=2`, a cancellation comment followed by one actual failure produces a streak of two and dispatches a report, although only one run failed.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_phase_report.sh:Lines 123-125 fetch comment bodies; `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:692` treats matching success prefixes as streak terminators without checking the comment author. | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A user-authored comment beginning with a success prefix, such as `The task appears clear.`, resets the phase failure streak.
  WHY: When the configured threshold is above one, a user can post a matching comment between failures and prevent the next failure from reaching the reporting threshold.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:`PHASE_SUCCESS_COMMENT_PREFIXES` at lines 134-139; successful implementation marks the issue `ai:done` at `.github/workflows/implement.yml:5240-5252` but does not post a success comment on the issue. | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Successful implementation runs do not terminate the implementation failure streak.
  WHY: After an implementation failure, a successful implementation, and a later implementation failure on the same issue, the reporter still counts both failures. With a threshold of two, it reports a streak even though the failures were not consecutive.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:Lines 244-251 add `(job log unavailable)` to `LOG_FILES` when fetching a job log fails; lines 304-313 use the phase fallback only when `LOG_FILES` is empty. | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When the job is identified but its log cannot be fetched, the promised `phase:<phase>_failed` fingerprint fallback is bypassed.
  WHY: The placeholder makes `LOG_FILES` nonempty, so the intake fingerprints the generic `no-error-lines` signature instead of the phase-specific fallback. Unreadable-log failures for the same workflow and failing step therefore lose the intended fingerprint distinction.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
